gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Newport's own US store listing for the Smart Battery Box, ChatGPT's best-overall pick, says '*Not compatible with lithium batteries' for the whole box. It also misses that the lithium-rated alternative ChatGPT showed, the LiTime Group 24/27/31 box, now $84.99 at LiTime, has only a 16A breaker, so a 50–60A trolling-motor breaker must be added separately.
standout_why: Compared against the cited Newport Smart Battery Box FAQs, Minn Kota's Battery Power Center page, and the top rivals paddleroundthepier.com and kayakguru.com. The Newport FAQ only says the LED battery meter 'is not compatible with Lithium batteries', and ChatGPT repeated it as 'battery-level indicator is not accurate for lithium'. Paddleroundthepier makes no lithium statement on the Newport and lists the LiTime breaker as not stated. Kayakguru names no lithium-compatible box and gives no breaker ratings. None of them has Newport's box-level 'not compatible with lithium' line or the LiTime's 16A-only breaker.
decides: This splits the pick by battery type. For lead-acid or AGM, the Newport Smart Battery Box ($69.99, 60A motor breaker) stays the pick. For a lithium (LiFePO4) trolling battery, like the Redodo 12V 100Ah trolling battery that Dealectric lists, Newport's own listing rules its box out. The lithium choice becomes the LiTime box at $84.99: it is rated for lithium and its interior (14 × 8.11 × 8.66 in) fits a 13 × 6.77 × 8.43 in Group 31 LiFePO4 battery. The buyer must add a 50–60A breaker sized to the motor, because the LiTime's 16A breaker doesn't protect the motor circuit.
